items.reason: "GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays."
"helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification" is marketing wording.
"Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines."
A statement is not overgeneral just because it says something is a challenge or is important.
It is a specific, checkable statement with no listed weaknesses.
It is a specific, checkable statement with no listed weaknesses.
It is a plain definition that is specific and checkable with no listed weaknesses.
"Engineers view hallucinations as an active research problem" makes a sweeping claim about what a whole group thinks.
The sentence is a specific, checkable statement with no hedging, promotional language, overgeneralization, unsupported causation, or missing sources.
The sentence provides a plain, direct definition of factual hallucinations without any disqualifying problems.
Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
It is a specific, checkable statement with no listed weaknesses.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: Citation checkers identify hallucinated references instantly to help educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.
claims.evidence_span: Our citation checker identifies these hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.

claims.claim_text: Source finder detects checkable, objective claims in text and matches those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.
claims.evidence_span: Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.

claims.claim_text: Detecting and mitigating errors and hallucinations pose significant challenges for practical deployment and reliability of large language models in high-stakes scenarios.
claims.evidence_span: Detecting and mitigating errors and hallucinations pose significant challenges for practical deployment and reliability of LLMs in high-stakes scenarios, such as chip design, supply chain logistics, and medical diagnostics.

claims.claim_text: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.
claims.evidence_span: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.

claims.claim_text: In October 2025, several hallucinations including non-existent academic sources and a fake quote from a federal court judgement were discovered in a report written by Deloitte and submitted to the Australian government.
claims.evidence_span: In October 2025, several hallucinations, including non-existent academic sources and a fake quote from a federal court judgement were discovered in an A$ 440,000 report written by Deloitte and submitted to the Australian government in July.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system which are either factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by any credible sources but sound coherent and fluent on the face of it.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system which are either factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by any credible sources but sound coherent and fluent on the face of it.

claims.claim_text: Engineers view hallucinations as an active research problem and a key barrier to reliable deployment, especially in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, legal and regulatory work.
claims.evidence_span: Engineers view hallucinations as an active research problem and a key barrier to reliable deployment, especially in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, legal and regulatory work.

claims.claim_text: Generative AI models are trained to produce outputs that look statistically credible in a certain modality.
claims.evidence_span: Generative AI models are trained to produce outputs that look statistically credible in a certain modality.

claims.claim_text: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.
claims.evidence_span: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.

claims.claim_text: Specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time according to Stanford research.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.

claims.claim_text: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
claims.evidence_span: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
